name: Scan Materials
description: Practice-theory op (T2R row 115): 'Where does the cue live in your environment?' Inventory the physical/digital environment description into practice_graph[].materials. The agent proposes rearrangements; the user rearranges. Cues supplement, not replace, practice.
guardrails: Materials inventory is descriptive — the agent proposes, the user rearranges.
Cues supplement, never replace, practice (T2R row 94).
No material change is proposed without a stated link to the target behavior.

name: Scan Meanings
description: Practice-theory op (T2R row 96): surface the user's framing of the activity into practice_graph[].meanings. Meaning-making is user-owned (Charter: preserve judgment); identity-level reframes require explicit confirmation (Phase 11 confirmed-Q2 path); the agent surfaces framings, never imposes them.
guardrails: Meanings are user-owned — the agent surfaces, never imposes.
Identity-level reframes (who the user IS) require explicit user confirmation before use (Phase 11 confirmed-Q2).
Framings are hypotheses with evidence anchors, never verdicts (Valens P4).

name: Detect Shared Elements
description: Practice-theory op (T2R row 116): detect bundles — one competence serving two practices, one material hosting two routines. Outputs the overlap map that makes rearrangement economical: change one element, benefit two practices.
guardrails: Shared-element detection is descriptive; proposals remain suggestions.
Overlap is reported with evidence anchors (which practices share what).
No element is claimed shared without appearing in two practices' inventories.

name: Design Novelty Into Routine
description: Practice-theory design op: propose material/arrangement changes that introduce novelty through arrangement, never by imposing meaning. Respects the 'cues ≠ replacement' rule and the user-owned-meaning boundary. Proposals are suggestions for the user to adopt or reject.
guardrails: Novelty enters via arrangement, never by imposing meaning.
Each proposal cites the material it changes and the practice it serves.
Proposals are suggestions — the user's arrangement authority is absolute.
